Mission clue. Imagine standing in sunlight and then in shade. What faraway object is sending the light?
Learn clue. The Moon travels around Earth.
Tiny iron-rich grains in Mars dust help give the planet its rusty colour.
Learn clue. People call Mars the Red Planet because some of its dust looks rusty.
You remembered this from before. Tiny iron-rich grains in Mars dust help give the planet its rusty colour.
A spacesuit gives astronauts air to breathe and helps keep their bodies safe.
Learn clue. A spacesuit gives an astronaut air to breathe and helps protect their body in space.
You remembered this from before. A spacesuit gives astronauts air to breathe and helps keep their bodies safe.
Solar panels change sunlight into electricity that can run spacecraft tools and systems.
Mission clue. Spacecraft need power for their lights, computers, and tools. What kind of power can sunlight provide?
You remembered this from before. Solar panels change sunlight into electricity that can run spacecraft tools and systems.
Rover wheels let the robot roll over rocky ground on Mars.
Mission clue. A rover rolls across Mars instead of flying. What job can its wheels help it do?
You remembered this from before. Rover wheels let the robot roll over rocky ground on Mars.
The Moon does not make its own light; it bounces sunlight back toward us.
Mission clue. Watch the Moon’s bright part over time. Which other bright object could be lighting it?
You remembered this from before. The Moon does not make its own light; it bounces sunlight back toward us.
Most of Earth’s surface is water that is not frozen; it is in the oceans.
Mission clue. Picture Earth from space. Compare the blue and brown areas: which choice covers the larger part?
You remembered this from before. Most of Earth’s surface is water that is not frozen; it is in the oceans.
Rover cameras take pictures so teams can study the ground and plan safe drives.
Mission clue. Before scientists plan a rover’s next move, what could help them see the ground ahead?
You remembered this from before. Rover cameras take pictures so teams can study the ground and plan safe drives.
Earth is almost a ball. It is a little wider around the middle.
Mission clue. Imagine Earth from far away. Which choice has a curved outside all around, without corners?
You remembered this from before. Earth is almost a ball. It is a little wider around the middle.
A rocket engine pushes hot gas downward. That push moves the rocket upward.
Mission clue. Let go of an inflated balloon without tying it. What comes out as the balloon darts away?
You remembered this from before. A rocket engine pushes hot gas downward. That push moves the rocket upward.
Earth’s atmosphere is the layer of gases around our planet.
Learn clue. The atmosphere is the layer of gases all around Earth.
You remembered this from before. Earth’s atmosphere is the layer of gases around our planet.
Mars has water ice at its north and south poles and in some places under its ground.
Mission clue. Water can stay frozen in very cold places. Think about the cold top and bottom ends of a planet, and places under its ground.
You remembered this from before. Mars has water ice at its north and south poles and in some places under its ground.
A heat shield is a protective covering that helps keep a spacecraft from getting too hot as it moves through a planet’s air.
Learn clue. A heat shield is a protective covering that helps keep a spacecraft from getting too hot as it moves through a planet’s air.
You remembered this from before. A heat shield is a protective covering that helps keep a spacecraft from getting too hot as it moves through a planet’s air.
A parachute catches air. The air pushes back and helps slow a lander as it comes down.
Mission clue. Watch what happens when a falling leaf spreads out and catches air. How might catching air slow something down?
You remembered this from before. A parachute catches air. The air pushes back and helps slow a lander as it comes down.
An antenna sends radio messages from a spacecraft. Equipment on Earth receives them.
Mission clue. A rover cannot drive its messages back to Earth. Which part might send them through space?
You remembered this from before. An antenna sends radio messages from a spacecraft. Equipment on Earth receives them.
Earth’s axis, the imaginary line it spins around, is tilted. As Earth goes around the Sun, the tilt changes which half gets more direct sunlight. That makes seasons.
Mission clue. Compare how directly sunlight shines on the top and bottom halves of Earth at different times of year.
You remembered this from before. Earth’s axis, the imaginary line it spins around, is tilted. As Earth goes around the Sun, the tilt changes which half gets more direct sunlight. That makes seasons.
How many small moons travel around Mars?
Rover cameras take pictures. The rover’s computer can use them to spot rocks and plan a safe route.
Mission clue. Before crossing a rocky patch, what could show the rover where the rock is?
You remembered this from before. Rover cameras take pictures. The rover’s computer can use them to spot rocks and plan a safe route.
Landing legs help a lander stand steadily and hold its weight on the ground.
Mission clue. Imagine a lander touching down on rough ground. How could strong legs help it stay upright?
You remembered this from before. Landing legs help a lander stand steadily and hold its weight on the ground.
An orbit is the path one object follows around another in space.
Learn clue. An orbit is the path one object follows around another in space.
You remembered this from before. An orbit is the path one object follows around another in space.
Radio messages take time to travel between Earth and Mars, so rovers follow some planned steps while they wait for the next message.

You remembered this from before. Radio messages take time to travel between Earth and Mars, so rovers follow some planned steps while they wait for the next message.
Venus has a very thick layer of gas around it. The gas carbon dioxide helps hold heat in.
Learn clue. Venus has very thick air that holds heat close to the planet.
You remembered this from before. Venus has a very thick layer of gas around it. The gas carbon dioxide helps hold heat in.
Learn clue. Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.
Scientists have evidence that Jupiter’s moon Europa may have salty water under its icy outer shell.
Learn clue. Europa is Jupiter’s icy moon. Scientists have evidence that salty water may be under its ice.
You remembered this from before. Scientists have evidence that Jupiter’s moon Europa may have salty water under its icy outer shell.
Mission clue. A wide parachute catches more air than a narrow one. What might catching more air do to a lander’s fall?
Some Mars rovers use a nuclear-powered system that turns heat into electricity when sunlight is limited.
Mission clue. Compare what a rover could use when sunlight is weak with what it could use near the bright Sun.
You remembered this from before. Some Mars rovers use a nuclear-powered system that turns heat into electricity when sunlight is limited.
Radio messages take several minutes to travel between Earth and Mars. The rover follows some planned steps while it waits for the next message.
Mission clue. A message to Mars travels much farther than a message across a room. Would both arrive right away?
You remembered this from before. Radio messages take several minutes to travel between Earth and Mars. The rover follows some planned steps while it waits for the next message.
Saturn’s rings are made mostly of bits of ice and rock.
Learn clue. Saturn is the planet famous for its bright rings.
You remembered this from before. Saturn’s rings are made mostly of bits of ice and rock.

Learn clue. NASA teams call one Mars day a sol.
You remembered this from before. NASA teams call one Mars day a sol. It lasts about 24 hours and 39 minutes.
Perseverance closes pieces of rock and soil in clean tubes so scientists can study them later. They may be brought back to Earth in a future mission.

You remembered this from before. Perseverance closes pieces of rock and soil in clean tubes so scientists can study them later. They may be brought back to Earth in a future mission.
Solar panels change sunlight into electricity. Mission planners choose a spacecraft’s power source based on where it travels.
Mission clue. Spacecraft near the Sun can collect more sunlight than spacecraft far away. Which choice can collect sunlight?
You remembered this from before. Solar panels change sunlight into electricity. Mission planners choose a spacecraft’s power source based on where it travels.
Venus spins in the opposite direction to most planets.
You remembered this from before. Venus spins in the opposite direction to most planets.
Perseverance uses pictures to make a map of nearby ground and avoid rocks.
Mission clue. Before a rover rolls ahead, what could show it where rocks and open ground are?
You remembered this from before. Perseverance uses pictures to make a map of nearby ground and avoid rocks.
